title: Aharonov-Bohm interference probing of chiral Andreev edge states via scanning gate microscopy
abstract: We theoretically investigate the spatial response of chiral Andreev edge states at a quantum Hall-superconductor interface probed by scanning gate microscopy. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism, we demonstrate that the localized potential of the scanning gate tip decouples the chiral Andreev edge states from the superconductor into independent electron and hole paths. In the $ν=2$ regime, this local separation forces the quasiparticles to accumulate a relative magnetic phase in the normal region, resulting in Aharonov-Bohm-type conductance oscillations that are captured by a geometric analytical model. At higher filling factors (e.g., $ν=4$), the tip progressively interacts with spatially distinct edge channels, dynamically altering the Andreev-induced mode mixing and modifying the transport resonances. Furthermore, we show that these highly localized interferometric signatures survive in the presence of disorder, even when conventional non-local transport oscillations are masked.
summary: This work theoretically models how chiral Andreev edge states behave when probed by a scanning gate microscope at a quantum Hall-superconductor interface. By analyzing the system using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism, the authors predict and demonstrate that the local tip potential induces Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in the conductance. This technique offers a robust method to characterize superconducting edge states, even when disorder is present.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates how chiral Andreev edge states (CAESs) at a quantum Hall-superconductor interface respond to local perturbations from a scanning gate microscope (SGM).
main_result: The SGM tip forces the electron and hole components of the CAESs to accumulate a relative magnetic phase, leading to observable Aharonov-Bohm-type conductance oscillations, which persist even in the presence of disorder.
method: The analysis uses the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism and the Landauer-Büttiker approach to calculate non-local conductance ($G$) as a function of the tip position.
model_or_system: The system is a Quantum Hall-Superconductor (QH-SC) hybrid structure. The physics is governed by the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian, incorporating the local potential of the SGM tip and the magnetic field via the vector potential.
key_observables:
Aharonov-Bohm-type conductance oscillations ($\Delta G$), probability current maps, and the dependence of oscillation amplitude on the filling factor ($
u$).

Filling factors ($

main_assumptions: Assumes negligible Zeeman interaction and spin degeneracy; the analysis often relies on approximating the tip potential and assuming adiabatic evolution of the edge states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate conductance maps ($\Delta G$) showing characteristic oscillations as the tip scans across the edge, and probability current maps demonstrating the decoupling of electron and hole paths.
paper_structure:
The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework (Bogoliubov-de Gennes model) to deriving the AB oscillation formula based on mode decoupling, demonstrating this effect for $
u=2$ and $
u=4$, and finally extending the analysis to show the robustness of the signature against disorder.
why_interesting: The ability to use a local probe (SGM) to map out fundamental quantum interference phenomena (AB effect) in superconducting edge states provides a powerful conceptual link between topological superconductivity and mesoscopic transport measurements.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic diagram of the QH-SC system. The light green part denotes the QH part, the gray region denotes the superconducting part and the yellow parts denote the semi- infinite normal leads. The electrons propagating on the QH edge mode forms CAES at the NS interface. We plot resulting probability current at the edge, where colors correspond to its electron (red) and hole (blue) character. The SGM tip, introduced in the system and denoted by the dark green color, locally perturbs the CAES at the QH-SC edge, detouring its path from the interface.
